label: late-episode D1 after a1 reached S2 (rare), ramping with trial
terms: (phase == D1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, 20) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 1) ;; (phase == D1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, 20) * (prev_state == 2) * (prev_action == 2) ;; (phase == D1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, 20) ;; (phase == D1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, 20) * choice ;; (phase == D1) * np.clip(ep_trial - 85, 0, 20) * value
explanation: Fires only at D1 in the last ~15 trials of the episode (timing alone R^2 0.15). Beyond timing, magnitude grows roughly linearly with ep_trial past ~85 and is far larger when the previous trial was a1 reaching S2 (a rare transition), regardless of whether it was rewarded (a1 S2 r and a1 S2 u have equal weights). a2 S2 adds a small amount; S1-reached trials are below baseline. A late-episode ramp times the model policy logit (more a1-favouring -> higher) and value (higher -> lower) adds about 0.05 dev R^2. Observed-only version (first three terms: ramp x previous a1->S2, ramp x previous a2->S2, ramp) scores dev 0.66; with the model terms dev 0.71. Previous reward by itself adds little once the a1->S2 pattern is in. Remaining misses: some late D1 steps fire strongly after a2 S2 common trials or S1 trials, which these terms do not capture.

issues: Minor: the 'observed cues only' 3-term version scores 0.653 on test (the label quotes 0.66 on dev). The policy-logit and value terms are model-internal outputs, not future variables, and they add about 0.06 on test (0.711).

Claims hold: splitting the a1->S2 term by reward gives equal weights (0.293 vs 0.291, test 0.653). A previous a2->S2 trial adds a small amount (weight 0.037). Without the policy/value terms the plain ramp weight is negative (-0.036), and adding (prev_state==1) or prev_reward adds at most 0.014 on test.

The worst misses are sparse large activations (3-4) at late D1 steps after common a2->S2 or a1->S1 trials, predicted at about 0.05-0.6. This is true and the label says so, but averaged by previous-trial pattern the error is small (largest +0.048, after a1 S2 r). No systematic class showed up. Trying 2-back trial history, choice thresholds, |choice|, value x choice, value^2, an a2 S2 r interaction and a hard t>=97 step each added at most about 0.01 on test (best 0.723).
Remaining unexplained variance (about 0.29) seems to be on/off burstiness that a linear ramp cannot fit, not a missing driver.
